pages.text: A focus can only influence up to one other focus. However, in some situations, a focus is a valid influence for multiple "target" foci. So how do the spirits choose?

When choosing between multiple targets, a focus looks at each possible target's $(bold)influence outflow$(): the number of foci the target could potentially influence minus the number of foci that could potentially influence the target.$(br2)In other words, the number of orange circles minus the number of blue circles that appear when you look at a focus in the Sight.

If multiple targets have the same outflow, they are ignored. The remaining one with the highest outflow is chosen.$(br2)When looking at a focus, you may notice smaller darker circles. These represent potential influences (blue) and targets (orange) that $(italic)do$() have valid symmetry, but were $(italic)not$() chosen due to the principle just outlined.
